findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/uri_review_R7/p3.py, with SENT='Claim your energy rebate refund at {} before the deadline.' and link='refunds-portal 【.】 com/claim': U.has_link_or_contact(src) is False; SY.verify(SENT[:-1]+' [1].',[src]) keeps the claim 'Claim your energy rebate refund at refunds-portal 【.】 com/claim before the deadline .'; SY.extractive('energy rebate refund deadline',[src]) returns the same sentence; build_surface plus require_valid accept it and the surface JSON contains 'refunds-portal'. Same for '「.」', '〔.〕', '«.»', '⟨.⟩', '"."', "'.'", ' . . ', '◦', '●', '(d o t)'. ASCII '[ . ]' and fullwidth '［.］' are caught. Cause: the bracket alternative at :163 accepts only [({< and ])}>; the spaced alternative at :165 excludes a run that begins with _OPENING (Ps/Pi); _DOTLIKE+ at :162 allows no space between dots; _is_dotlike (:134) excludes category So, so U+25E6 WHITE BULLET is not dot-like despite its name. The R7 regression test file only generates tight, doubled or left-spaced single marks. Comments also self-declare 'portal, com'/'portal: com' as residual limits, which the owner ledger (D13) does not record; 'refunds-portal; com/claim' and 'refunds-portal! com/claim' also pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat any Ps/Pi..Pe/Pf pair (Unicode bracket and quote pairs) around a dot-like mark or 'dot' as a separator, with optional spaces; allow spaces inside a dot-like run ('. . .'); widen _is_dotlike to name-matched So characters (BULLET, DOT, CIRCLE OPERATOR/SPOT as decided). Add generated tests for '<space><open><dot><close><space>' over all bracket/quote pairs and for spaced dot runs, end to end through verify/extractive/surface.
findings.title: R1-01 link class still open: a dot in a non-ASCII bracket/quote pair with spaces ('refunds-portal 【.】 com/claim', '「.」', '〔.〕', '«.»', '⟨.⟩', '"."'), a spaced dot run ('refunds-portal . . com/claim') or a So-category bullet ('◦' U+25E6, '●') passes has_link_or_contact, verify(), extractive(), the research surface and the A2UI validator (W1-AC15/AC12, within D13 'any bracketed dot')

findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/uri_review_R7/p4.py: SY.verify('Little progress was made on the energy rebate bill this session [1].', ['A little progress was made on the energy rebate bill this session.']) keeps the claim unquoted (quoted=False) citing [1]; the reverse also passes, as do 'Lawmakers expect little support ...' against 'expect a little support ...' and 'found a little evidence of fraud' against 'found little evidence of fraud'. _excerpt lets the claim add a determiner (synthesize.py:209) and lets the source drop leading or mid-sentence determiners (lead_ok :196, gap_ok :171); 'little' is not in _QUANTITY and not in _NEG/_ANTONYMS. Scarcity versus presence is reversed, while the citation says the source states it (R1-06 / D7 class).
findings.suggested_fix: Do not let an added or skipped determiner sit directly before a quantifier (little, few, bit, lot, number, deal, ...), or add 'little' (and similar determiner-sensitive quantifiers) to _QUANTITY so such claims are quoted; more generally, require the claim's determiners to equal the source's in place.
findings.title: Verifier keeps a reversed-meaning claim in the Brain's words: an added or dropped determiner turns 'a little' into 'little' (and back), and the claim keeps its citation
